recommended_change.label: pinned-stack+lean-kernel-cmdline
host_commands:
cat > /etc/systemd/system/dnstune.sh <<'EOF'
#!/bin/bash
cmp -s /users/ckranig/multi_record/db.workbench.lan /etc/bind/db.workbench.lan || cp /users/ckranig/multi_record/db.workbench.lan /etc/bind/db.workbench.lan
for g in /sys/devices/system/cpu/cpu*/cpufreq/scaling_governor; do echo performance > $g; done
for s in /sys/devices/system/cpu/cpu*/cpuidle/state3/disable /sys/devices/system/cpu/cpu*/cpuidle/state4/disable; do echo 1 > $s; done
echo always > /sys/kernel/mm/transparent_hugepage/enabled
echo 5000000 > /sys/kernel/debug/sched/migration_cost_ns
ethtool -G eno4 rx 2040
sleep 3
ethtool -C eno4 rx-usecs 100 rx-frames 64 rx-usecs-irq 100 rx-frames-irq 64 tx-usecs 200 tx-frames 64 tx-usecs-irq 200 tx-frames-irq 64
ethtool -K eno4 gro off
sysctl -w net.core.default_qdisc=pfifo_fast
tc qdisc replace dev eno4 root mq
for q in 0 1 2 3 4 5 6 7; do printf '%x' $((1<<q)) > /sys/class/net/eno4/queues/tx-$q/xps_cpus; done
systemctl stop irqbalance
for q in 0 1 2 3 4 5 6 7; do irq=$(awk -v n=eno4-$q '$NF==n {sub(":","",$1); print $1}' /proc/interrupts); [ -n "$irq" ] && echo $q > /proc/irq/$irq/smp_affinity_list; done
systemctl --no-block stop collectl apache2 packagekit
exit 0
EOF

sed -i 's/^GRUB_CMDLINE_LINUX_DEFAULT=.*/GRUB_CMDLINE_LINUX_DEFAULT="mitigations=off cpufreq.default_governor=performance apparmor=0 init_on_alloc=0 hardened_usercopy=off cgroup.memory=nokmem audit=0 nowatchdog"/' /etc/default/grub

recommended_apply_script:
#!/bin/bash
# pinned-stack+lean-kernel-cmdline
set -e

# Add to the options block of /etc/bind/named.conf.options:
#     udp-receive-buffer 16777216;
#     udp-send-buffer 16777216;
#     reuseport no;
#     zone-statistics none;
#     querylog no;

cp /users/ckranig/multi_record/db.workbench.lan /etc/bind/db.workbench.lan && chown root:bind /etc/bind/db.workbench.lan && chmod 644 /etc/bind/db.workbench.lan
printf 'net.core.rmem_max=16777216\nnet.core.rmem_default=16777216\nnet.core.wmem_max=16777216\nnet.core.wmem_default=4194304\nnet.core.netdev_max_backlog=30000\nnet.core.default_qdisc=pfifo_fast\nkernel.sched_autogroup_enabled=0\n' > /etc/sysctl.d/99-dnsperf.conf
mkdir -p /etc/systemd/system/named.service.d && printf '[Service]\nEnvironment=MALLOC_CONF=thp:always,metadata_thp:always\n' > /etc/systemd/system/named.service.d/thp.conf
cat > /etc/systemd/system/dnstune.sh <<'EOF'
#!/bin/bash
cmp -s /users/ckranig/multi_record/db.workbench.lan /etc/bind/db.workbench.lan || cp /users/ckranig/multi_record/db.workbench.lan /etc/bind/db.workbench.lan

sleep 3

for q in 0 1 2 3 4 5 6 7; do printf '%x' $((1<<q)) > /sys/class/net/eno4/queues/tx-$q/xps_cpus; done
systemctl stop irqbalance
for q in 0 1 2 3 4 5 6 7; do irq=$(awk -v n=eno4-$q '$NF==n {sub(":","",$1); print $1}' /proc/interrupts); [ -n "$irq" ] && echo $q > /proc/irq/$irq/smp_affinity_list; done

exit 0

printf '[Unit]\nDescription=dns tune\nAfter=network-online.target\nWants=network-online.target\nBefore=named.service\n[Service]\nType=oneshot\nExecStart=/bin/bash /etc/systemd/system/dnstune.sh\nRemainAfterExit=yes\n[Install]\nWantedBy=multi-user.target\n' > /etc/systemd/system/dnstune.service
systemctl daemon-reload
systemctl enable dnstune.service
sed -i 's/^GRUB_CMDLINE_LINUX_DEFAULT=.*/GRUB_CMDLINE_LINUX_DEFAULT="mitigations=off cpufreq.default_governor=performance apparmor=0 init_on_alloc=0 hardened_usercopy=off cgroup.memory=nokmem audit=0 nowatchdog"/' /etc/default/grub
update-grub

sudo systemctl reboot
summary:
RECOMMENDATION: pinned-stack-lean-kernel-cmdline__a7d558aec8, which scored 260k QPS. Baseline was 170k, so that is +53%.

Configuration:
- named.conf.options:
  - udp-receive-buffer 16777216;
  - udp-send-buffer 16777216;
  - reuseport no;
  - zone-statistics none;
  - querylog no;
- Sysctls: rmem/wmem max 16M, netdev_max_backlog 30000, default_qdisc pfifo_fast, sched_autogroup 0.
- Kernel command line: mitigations=off cpufreq.default_governor=performance apparmor=0 init_on_alloc=0 hardened_usercopy=off cgroup.memory=nokmem audit=0 nowatchdog.
- A oneshot unit that runs before named:
  - performance governor; C3/C6 disabled; THP always (plus MALLOC_CONF=thp:always for named)
  - eno4: rx ring 2040; rx coalescing 100us/64 frames, tx 200us/64 frames; GRO off
  - mq root qdisc with pfifo_fast children; XPS CPU i -> tx-i; irqbalance stopped, IRQ vector i pinned to CPU i
  - collectl, apache2 and packagekit stopped.

CONFIDENCE: moderate. The 260k point was measured once. Its confirmation repeat (the last of the budget) ended as a harness "failed" with no levels, as had one earlier run; neither produced data. Evidence that the gain is real anyway: every overload level moved up about 3 points against four earlier runs of the same stack without the lean command line (270k 96.2% vs 91-94%, 300k 85.7% vs 81-83.6%, 400k 63.5% vs 60-61.6%). Repeat noise at fixed levels is otherwise about 1 point. Expect 250-260k; I would not promise 260k on every boot. Without the lean command line the stack measured 250, 250, 250, 230 and 250k.

WHAT LIMITS THIS SERVER: CPU in named itself. The hardware is a 4-core/8-thread Xeon E5530 (Nehalem) with a bnx2 1GbE NIC.
- All loss is UDP receive-buffer overflow. NIC drops (rx_fw_discards) and backlog drops were zero in the monitored runs.
- At the knee there is no idle CPU: about 78% user (BIND), 19% sys, 14% softirq.
- Saturated goodput is about 255-260k answers/s; at 400k offered it still answers about 250k.
- The BIND profile is flat (ns__client_setup, qp-trie lookup, message render, stats counters); there is no single hot spot left to remove.

Biggest lessons:
1. bnx2 RSS hashes on IP only. With 2 client IPs, only 2 RX queues and 2 CPUs get receive traffic, and which queues get it changes from boot to boot. With reuseport, each worker owns 1/8 of the flows, so the workers sharing CPUs with softirq overflow first. `reuseport no` (one shared socket, workers self-balance) gave 180k -> 220k, the largest single win.
2. Kernel overhead cuts: mitigations=off (Nehalem has no PCID) about +4%. AppArmor off, coalescing and service trimming about +5%. XPS with pfifo_fast removed TX queue/qdisc contention from the single socket, about +4%. The lean command line (init_on_alloc etc.) about +3%.
3. Not useful: 4 worker threads (-n 4) scored 190k, so hyperthreads help. UDP early demux off had no effect. rp_filter=0 had no measurable effect.

HARNESS PITFALL: after each restore reboot, the testbed provisioning (install_all_ns.sh) copies a 10-line default db.workbench.lan over the 3.5 MB benchmark zone. Every query then answers NXDOMAIN and the run scores 0. Runs 5 and 10 were lost to this. My configs work around it by copying /users/ckranig/multi_record/db.workbench.lan back into /etc/bind before named starts. Any future campaign needs this or a harness fix.

STATE: residual drift was only IRQ renumbering of another device after reboot. The final restored server has the default command line, named active, and the large zone in place. Files I left behind are /tmp/sampler.sh and /tmp/prof.sh, plus perf data, pcaps and logs (/tmp/*.data, /var/tmp/dnsprof*, /var/tmp/mon.log). They don't affect measurements.

NEXT STEPS:
- Repeat the winner 2-3 times.
- Make RX placement deterministic across boots: put the RSS target queues on fixed CPUs, or test RPS to spread receive processing.
- Try BIND build or version options: a newer 9.20 or 9.21 build, or one built without stats.
- A NIC with 4-tuple UDP RSS would let reuseport scale.
- At this point the remaining gains need less per-query CPU in BIND, not more kernel tuning.
